newsitem.title: DENMARK: Tele Danmark buys back A-shares.
newsitem.headline: Tele Danmark buys back A-shares.

text.p: Danish state-run telecoms group Tele Danmark said on Monday that it was implementing as planned its previously announced programme to buy back its A-shares, due to be phased out next year.

"The Danish state will, on March 1 1997, redeem all privately held A-shares at a price of 125 Danish crowns per share of a nominal value of 100 crowns. The redemption will not incur any expenses on the part of the shareholders," a company statement said.
Holders of the shares would receive dividends covering 1996 and two months of 1997, it added.

In a move first announced in February 1996, each A share of 100 crowns is to split into 10 shares of 10 crowns each from June 1 1998 when the two classes of share become equal and the A and B designations will cease.
The manoeuvre slightly raises the state' share of the company, partially privatised in 1994, to 51.73 percent from 51.00 percent.

The government, pledged to balance the public-sector budget and reduce foreign debt, has said that it does not see itself retaining control of the group indefinitely but would not sell any shares in 1997.
It does not say when further privatisation is likely although 1998, as well as seeing the share rationalisation, is also scheduled to be an election year.
